subject: ARA
label: Grade 07
task: Meet the outcome of every unit in Grade 07 Arabic, and keep one piece of evidence for each.
condition: A 36-week school year, 4 units, a teacher or guide, a learning book or device, and local examples in the local language first with English support.
standard: Each unit: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer. Course pass: no unit at 'Not yet' after one retry, and a pass in SA1 and SA2.

modules.title: Reading short stories
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Reading short stories', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: summarise a short story. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Reading short stories' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: summarise a short story, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: الولد يلعب في الحديقة. أين يلعب الولد؟ في الحديقة. (The boy plays in the garden. Where does the boy play? In the garden.) Method: Model run for 'Reading short stories'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Summarise a short story: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Read the story I wrote. كَانَ فِي قَرْيَةٍ صَغِيرَةٍ صَبِيٌّ اسْمُهُ يُوسُفُ يَخَافُ مِنَ الظَّلَامِ. فِي لَيْلَةٍ انْقَطَعَ النُّورُ، فَأَشْعَلَ شَمْعَةً وَسَاعَدَ جَارَتَهُ الْعَجُوزَ. [In a small village there was a boy named Yusuf who feared the dark. One night the electricity went out, so he lit a candle and helped his old neighbour.]

Step 2, Read the ending. عِنْدَهَا عَرَفَ أَنَّ الشَّجَاعَةَ أَنْ نَفْعَلَ الْخَيْرَ رَغْمَ الْخَوْفِ. [Then he knew that courage is to do good in spite of fear.] Underline the lesson sentence, which tells you what the story teaches.

Step 3, List the story elements. الشَّخْصِيَّاتُ [characters]: يُوسُفُ وَالْجَارَةُ. الْمَكَانُ [place]: قَرْيَةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ. الْمُشْكِلَةُ [problem]: الْخَوْفُ مِنَ الظَّلَامِ. الْحَلُّ [solution]: شَمْعَةٌ وَمُسَاعَدَةٌ. الْعِبْرَةُ [lesson]: الشَّجَاعَةُ فِعْلُ الْخَيْرِ. Fill in each from the text.

Step 4, Write a three-sentence summary. يُحْكَى عَنْ صَبِيٍّ يَخَافُ مِنَ الظَّلَامِ. فِي لَيْلَةٍ انْقَطَعَ النُّورُ فَسَاعَدَ جَارَتَهُ بِشَمْعَةٍ. تَعَلَّمَ أَنَّ الشَّجَاعَةَ فِعْلُ الْخَيْرِ. [It is told of a boy who feared the dark. One night, when the light went out, he helped his neighbour with a candle. He learned that courage is doing good.]

Step 5, Fix an error. A student retells every detail, including the village size, and adds an opinion. Correction: a summary keeps only the main events in your own words, in the past tense, and leaves out opinions. Aim for about a third of the text.

Step 6, Your turn: write two sentences on why the neighbour needed Yusuf and what he learned. Model answer: كَانَتِ الْجَارَةُ الْعَجُوزُ تَحْتَاجُ إِلَى النُّورِ. تَعَلَّمَ يُوسُفُ أَنْ يَتَغَلَّبَ عَلَى خَوْفِهِ. [The old neighbour needed light. Yusuf learned to overcome his fear.]

modules.title: Present and past tenses
modules.outcome: use verbs in present and past
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Present and past tenses', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: use verbs in present and past. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Present and past tenses' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: use verbs in present and past, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: أكتب الدرس (present) ثم كتبتُ الدرس (past). يذهب تصبح ذهب. (writes becomes wrote; goes becomes went.) Method: Model run for 'Present and past tenses'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Use verbs in present and past: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Learn the past forms of كَتَبَ [to write]. كَتَبْتُ [I wrote], كَتَبْتَ [you wrote, m], كَتَبْتِ [you wrote, f], كَتَبَ [he wrote], كَتَبَتْ [she wrote], كَتَبْنَا [we wrote]. The endings are added to the stem كَتَب.

Step 2, Learn the present forms. أَكْتُبُ [I write], تَكْتُبُ [you write, m], تَكْتُبِينَ [you write, f], يَكْتُبُ [he writes], تَكْتُبُ [she writes], نَكْتُبُ [we write]. The prefixes أ ت ي ن show the person.

Step 3, Use time words. أَمْسِ كَتَبْتُ رِسَالَةً. [Yesterday I wrote a letter.] الْآنَ أَكْتُبُ وَاجِبِي. [Now I am writing my homework.] غَدًا سَأَكْتُبُ مَقَالًا. [Tomorrow I will write an essay.] Add سَـ before the present verb to make it future.

Step 4, Try another verb, ذَهَبَ [to go]. ذَهَبْنَا إِلَى الْمَكْتَبَةِ أَمْسِ. [We went to the library yesterday.] هِيَ تَذْهَبُ إِلَى الْمَدْرَسَةِ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. [She goes to school every day.] Say the past and present of both verbs for three persons.

Step 5, Fix errors. A student says هِيَ كَتَبَ الدَّرْسَ. Correction: هِيَ كَتَبَتِ الدَّرْسَ, because she needs the feminine ending ـَتْ. Another says نَحْنُ ذَهَبْتُ; correction: نَحْنُ ذَهَبْنَا, because we ends with ـنَا.

Step 6, Your turn: write one past and one present sentence with the verb قَرَأَ [to read]. Model answer: أَمْسِ قَرَأْتُ قِصَّةً. الْآنَ أَقْرَأُ كِتَابًا. [Yesterday I read a story. Now I am reading a book.] Check that قَرَأْتُ ends in تُ for I.

modules.title: Telephone and daily conversation
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Telephone and daily conversation', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: hold a short phone conversation. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Telephone and daily conversation' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: hold a short phone conversation, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: — السلام عليكم، هل أستطيع التحدث إلى أحمد؟ — وعليكم السلام، لحظة من فضلك. (Hello, may I speak to Ahmed? One moment please.) Method: Model run for 'Telephone and daily conversation'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Hold a short phone conversation: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, Open a call politely. أَلُو، السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. [Hello, peace be upon you.] هَلْ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَتَكَلَّمَ مَعَ سَلْمَى؟ [May I speak with Salma?] The reply is وَعَلَيْكُمُ السَّلَامُ. مَنْ يَتَكَلَّمُ؟ [And upon you peace. Who is speaking?]

Step 2, Say who you are. أَنَا خَالِدٌ، زَمِيلُهَا فِي الصَّفِّ. [I am Khalid, her classmate.] نَعَمْ، لَحْظَةً مِنْ فَضْلِكَ. [Yes, one moment please.] عُذْرًا، سَلْمَى غَيْرُ مَوْجُودَةٍ الْآنَ. [Sorry, Salma is not here now.]

Step 3, Leave a message. هَلْ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَتْرُكَ رِسَالَةً؟ [Do you want to leave a message?] نَعَمْ، أَخْبِرْهَا أَنَّ الِاجْتِمَاعَ غَدًا. [Yes, tell her the meeting is tomorrow.] حَسَنًا، سَأُخْبِرُهَا. [Fine, I will tell her.]

Step 4, Close the call. شُكْرًا جَزِيلًا. مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ. [Thank you very much. Goodbye.] If you dialled wrongly: عُذْرًا، الرَّقْمُ خَطَأٌ. [Sorry, wrong number.] Act out the full call with a partner, then swap roles.

Step 5, Fix an error. A caller says هَلْ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَتْرُكُ رِسَالَةً؟ with damma. Correction: هَلْ تُرِيدُ أَنْ تَتْرُكَ رِسَالَةً؟ because after أَنْ the verb takes fatha. Also never hang up without saying مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ.

Step 6, Your turn: phone a friend to ask about homework. Model answer: السَّلَامُ عَلَيْكُمْ. أَنَا نُورُ. هَلْ أَسْتَطِيعُ أَنْ أَسْأَلَ عَنِ الْوَاجِبِ؟ شُكْرًا. مَعَ السَّلَامَةِ. [Peace be upon you. I am Nour. May I ask about the homework? Thank you. Goodbye.]

modules.title: Descriptive writing
modules.intro: In this unit you work on 'Descriptive writing', taught in a way that is with notes, a worked line and a self-mark. The target is clear: describe a person or place. You move from seeing it, to saying it, to doing it alone.
points: Listen first: your teacher or a recording says the new words or sentences from 'Descriptive writing' twice. You repeat them aloud.
Notice the pattern: find where the new sound, word form or sentence rule appears in a short text and mark it.
Use it: describe a person or place, first with help, then alone.
Check and fix: read your work aloud once more; fix one thing you hear is wrong.
modules.example: Solved: فقرة: القراءة مفيدة. فهي تزيد معلوماتنا. وتنمّي لغتنا. لذلك أقرأ كل يوم. (topic sentence, two details, closing) Method: Model run for 'Descriptive writing'. Teacher text (3 lines about a daily activity). Step 1, read it aloud together. Step 2, mark every word or sentence that uses the new pattern. Step 3, a learner writes or says two new lines of their own that use the same pattern. Step 4, the learner reads them aloud and corrects one slip. What a good answer looks like: the pattern is used correctly in both lines, the lines make sense, and the learner can say which part is the pattern.
modules.activity: About 30 to 40 minutes of class work, then one short practice task for home. Keep evidence: a worked task and a corrected copy.
modules.standard: Describe a person or place: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer.
steps: Step 1, A description has three parts: appearance, character, example. For a person write: جَدِّي رَجُلٌ طَوِيلُ الْقَامَةِ، أَبْيَضُ الشَّعْرِ. [My grandfather is a tall man with white hair.] Notice طَوِيلُ الْقَامَةِ [tall of stature] is a common phrase.

Step 2, Add character. هُوَ هَادِئٌ وَكَرِيمٌ. [He is calm and generous.] يَبْتَسِمُ دَائِمًا. [He always smiles.] Choose adjectives that agree: for a woman say جَدَّتِي امْرَأَةٌ طَيِّبَةٌ [My grandmother is a kind woman].

Step 3, Give an example that proves the character. فِي كُلِّ جُمْعَةٍ يُوزِّعُ الْحَلْوَى عَلَى الْأَطْفَالِ. [Every Friday he gives out sweets to the children.] Connect with لِذَلِكَ [therefore]: لِذَلِكَ يُحِبُّهُ الْجَمِيعُ. [Therefore everyone loves him.]

Step 4, Describe a place. مَدِينَتِي سَاحِلِيَّةٌ صَغِيرَةٌ. شَوَارِعُهَا نَظِيفَةٌ وَبُيُوتُهَا بَيْضَاءُ. يَبْدُو الْبَحْرُ كَأَنَّهُ مِرْآةٌ كَبِيرَةٌ. [My town is a small coastal town. Its streets are clean and its houses white. The sea looks like a big mirror.] The word كَأَنَّ makes a simile.

Step 5, Fix an error. A student writes a list: طَوِيلٌ، كَرِيمٌ، هَادِئٌ. Correction: join the ideas in sentences and give an example, as in جَدِّي كَرِيمٌ لِأَنَّهُ يُسَاعِدُ الْفُقَرَاءَ [My grandfather is generous because he helps the poor]. Also agree adjectives with the noun.

Step 6, Your turn: describe your mother in three sentences. Model answer: أُمِّي امْرَأَةٌ جَمِيلَةٌ وَهَادِئَةٌ. تَعْمَلُ بِجِدٍّ كُلَّ يَوْمٍ. لِذَلِكَ أُحِبُّهَا كَثِيرًا. [My mother is a beautiful, calm woman. She works hard every day. Therefore I love her very much.]

rubric: Explains the idea to someone else
Practises most days and keeps evidence
checks: Unit 1 (Reading short stories): show that you can summarise a short story. What are the first and last step you used?

Any correct example is fine. A good answer names the first step (see or say the idea) and the last step (check or reflect) from the model run, and meets the standard: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer. (Covered in unit 1: Reading short stories.)

(Covered in unit 3: Telephone and daily conversation.)
Unit 4 (Descriptive writing): show that you can describe a person or place. What are the first and last step you used?

Any correct example is fine. A good answer names the first step (see or say the idea) and the last step (check or reflect) from the model run, and meets the standard: at least 8 of 10 marks on a short task, with one line of reasoning for each answer. (Covered in unit 4: Descriptive writing.)
Which action verb starts the outcome of Unit 1 (Reading short stories), and at which Bloom level is it?
'summarise', at the Understand level. (Covered in unit 1: Reading short stories.)
When do the formative checks FA1 to FA4 and the summative checks SA1 and SA2 happen?
FA1 to FA4 around weeks 6, 12, 24 and 30; SA1 in week 18; SA2 in week 36. (Covered in: Assessment plan, near the top of this page.)
In which weeks does Unit 4 (Descriptive writing) run?
Weeks 28 to 36. (Covered in unit 4: Descriptive writing.)
What evidence do you keep for each unit, and why?
A worked task and a corrected copy. It shows what you can really do and lets a teacher check it against the standard. (Covered in: How you are checked, further down this page.)
ladder: L1: say and read familiar words and short sentences.
L2: read short texts and write connected sentences.
L3: write paragraphs and speak on a topic with notes.
L4: write for different purposes and analyse how texts persuade.
L5: write and argue at length; handle unseen texts.
L6 (degree): academic reading, writing and citation.
L7 (postgraduate): publish, teach or translate with expert accuracy.
